title: scorecard-sensitivity-scenarios-and-action-runbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for running weighted health-score sensitivity experiments and mapping the most common risk-signal permutations to concrete CS actions. Goal is to produce a repeatable process for:
- tuning weights for the unified health score,
- validating thresholds that trigger QBR/renewal/outreach, and
- codifying the immediate playbook for each risk cluster.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focus: enterprise+midmarket accounts with Dedicated or Private plans (we may later generalize to self-serve).
- Data sources: Product telemetry (API calls, model route usage), Billing/contract data, Support tickets, NPS, Onboarding checklist completions.
- Baseline scoring model currently in use: "baseline-v1" (linked above). This doc explores sensitivity around weights + threshold choices.
- This is a draft: expect follow-ups from Data Eng (CS-421) and PMs.

Quick primer: how the score is computed (baseline)
- Signals (normalized 0..1): adoption_rate, active_routes, avg_latency_pctile, support_volume_per_week, feature_gap_index, contract_coverage, eval_regressions_count (normalized).
- Baseline weights (example): adoption_rate: 0.30, active_routes: 0.20, support_volume: 0.18, avg_latency_pctile: 0.12, contract_coverage: 0.10, feature_gap_index: 0.06, eval_regressions_count: 0.04
- HealthScore = (sum_i weight_i * signal_i) / (sum weights) * 100 (report scaled 0-100)
- Thresholds (draft): >=75 Green, 50-74 Yellow, <50 Red

Why sensitivity tests: common issues
- Small changes to high-weight signals (adoption_rate) can flip accounts from Yellow->Red. We need to know which accounts are brittle.
- Some signals are noisy (support tickets) and overreaction causes wasted AE/CS cycles.
- Different account segments (platform vs. product teams) respond differently to the same signals.

Planned experiments (A/B style)
Experiment 1 — High-adoption robust scenario (A1)
- Change: reduce adoption_rate weight from 0.30 -> 0.20 and distribute 0.10 across active_routes/support_volume equally.
- Hypothesis: fewer false positives in Red for platform accounts that have spiky usage but strong contracts.
- Metrics to collect: number of accounts changing risk bucket, precision/recall vs. historical churn, manual review false positives.

Experiment 2 — Noise dampening for support (B1)
- Change: apply a 7-day exponential smoothing to support_volume signal before normalization and reduce weight from 0.18 -> 0.12.
- Hypothesis: reduces reactive outreach on transient incidents.
- Metrics: outreach volume reduction, renewal outcomes for accounts flagged previously due to support spikes.

Experiment 3 — Contract-aware thresholds (C1)
- Change: for accounts with contract_coverage >=0.9, add +5 points to HealthScore before bucket assignment (soft bias toward Green).
- Hypothesis: prioritizes accounts with economic commitment; avoids wasting time on low-dollar churn.

Experiment 4 — Latency penalty for SLAs (D1)
- Change: increase avg_latency_pctile weight from 0.12 -> 0.18 for accounts with SLA clauses.
- Hypothesis: latency issues matter more for SLA customers and better predicts renewal.

Sensitivity analysis process (how we run these experiments)
1) Snapshot baseline scores for last 12 months for a representative cohort (n=800 accounts: 60% enterprise, 40% mid-market).
2) Run weighted recalculation for each experiment and produce delta table (account, baseline_score, new_score, delta, bucket_change).
3) Flag accounts with delta > 8 points and any bucket change for manual review.
4) Run outcome correlation: Did flagged accounts churn or renew historically? compute precision@k for predicted risk.
5) Weekly sync with PM/Analytics to decide winners (2–3 week iteration).

Example output snippet (text table):
account_id | baseline_score | expA1_score | delta | baseline_bucket -> expA1_bucket
REDW-042   | 58            | 51         | -7    | Yellow -> Yellow
ACCT-391   | 62            | 48         | -14   | Green -> Red
PLAT-88    | 80            | 76         | -4    | Green -> Green

Risk clusters and immediate actions
- Cluster: Low adoption + rising support volume (AdoptDrop)
  - Detection: adoption_rate <0.4 AND support_volume normalized >0.6 AND HealthScore delta < -10 after smoothing
  - Immediate action (0-48h): Triage ticket, AE reach out to confirm roadmap blockers, propose dedicated onboarding session.
  - 7-day action: Engagement plan + usage playbook; schedule technical audit (solutions-eng).
  - Escalation: If no adoption lift in 30 days, flag for renewal-focused QBR and additional pricing incentives.

- Cluster: Contracted SLA latency breach (LatencySLA)
  - Detection: avg_latency_pctile >0.9 for SLA accounts OR >0.95 repeated 3x in 14 days.
  - Immediate action (0-24h): notify SRE + assigned AE; open P0 incident; temporary routing fallback if available.
  - 7-day: detailed incident report to customer + timeline for mitigation, credit discussion if warranted.
  - Escalation: If unresolved >21 days, move to Executive QBR and Sales lead involvement.

- Cluster: Feature-gap / roadmap mismatch (FeatureGap)
  - Detection: feature_gap_index >0.7 AND product-contactless signals (low code commits, low route variance).
  - Action: Solutions engineering to build small PoC within 2–3 weeks or propose alternative integration patterns.

Mapping Risk -> Outreach templates (examples to copy/paste)
- Low adoption template (short):
  Subject: Quick check-in + 30-min session to unblock product usage
  Body: Hi <name>, noticed usage dipped on X. Could we hop on a 30-min call to review blockers and quick wins?

- Latency SLA template (incidents):
  Subject: Incident update & mitigation plan
  Body: Hi <name>, we’ve identified the root cause for higher latencies affecting route Y. Here’s immediate mitigation and ETA for full fix...

Data checks and observability notes (Data Eng tasks)
- Normalize signals against rolling 90-day window (add this to spec).
- Backfill smoothed support_volume for last 24 months.
- Expose per-customer signal time-series to CS dashboard for manual inspection (confluence ticket created).
- Add a flag column: "weight_sensitivity_brittle" for accounts where +/-10% weight change flips bucket.

Open questions / TODOs
- How do we treat multi-entity customers (several contracts under one parent)? Do we score at entity or parent? (Action: decide in Nov 10 sync).
- Should we incorporate qualitative signals (AE sentiment score) even though it's sparse? (Ravi to prototype).
- Do we want separate scoring models per vertical (adtech vs. fintech)? Initial plan: run A/B on two strata in Experiment scheduling.
- KPI for success of sensitivity tuning: 10% improvement in precision for Red->actual churn over 90 days.

Next steps (immediate)
- Maya: schedule 45-min sync with Analytics + Data Eng (CS-421) to agree on cohort and rollout dates (week of Oct 6).
- Jordan: spin up experiment pipelines, add smoothing function; initial run in sandbox by Oct 10.
- Elena: draft outreach templates in Sales/CS template repo; link to doc.
- Ravi: prototype AE sentiment ingest (Slack tag parser).

Notes to reviewers: this doc mixes working hypotheses and action items. Please add comments inline or link to JIRA-CS-421 for tracked tasks. If you iterate on weights, please append a short rationale and date to the top of the doc.

Appendix: quick checklist for running a sensitivity batch
- [ ] Export last 12 months baseline signals (include raw and normalized).
- [ ] Validate normalization pipelines, capture outliers.
- [ ] Run weight-shift scenarios and create delta buckets.
- [ ] Surface top 50 brittle accounts for manual review.
- [ ] Decide which experiments to promote to production (criteria: >8pt improvement in precision or reduction in false-positive outreach by 20%).
